title: `action-param-dialog` renders a hardcoded English `Select...` placeholder — untranslated in zh, and ASCII after #3878 moved the packs to U+2026
body:
Found while executing #4377 (the metadata-admin designer table's ellipsis convergence), on branch `claude/issue-4377-designer-table-ellipsis`. Out of that card's scope — its dispatch scoped the change to `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` alone — so recorded separately.

## The line

`packages/components/src/custom/action-param-dialog.tsx:198` — the `placeholder` prop passed to the `SelectValue` inside the `select` branch's `SelectTrigger`:

```tsx
placeholder={param.placeholder || 'Select...'}
```

(The full JSX element is written here without its opening angle bracket on purpose: GitHub's body sanitizer strips `<` followed by a letter, and it silently ate this snippet on the first save of this issue.)

The fallback fires whenever an action parameter of kind `select` declares no `placeholder` of its own, which is the ordinary case for hand-written action metadata.

## Two defects on one literal

1. **It is hardcoded English.** `action-param-dialog.tsx` imports no translation hook at all — `grep` for `useObjectTranslation` / `useTranslation` / `@object-ui/i18n` over the file returns nothing — so a zh-CN user opening an action's parameter dialog sees `Select...` in an otherwise Chinese dialog. This is the hardcoded-English family (#4024 and siblings); the sibling cases named there are different sites, and this one is not covered by any of them.
2. **The ellipsis is ASCII.** #3878 converged the ten locale packs on U+2026 `…` per the consistency pass on objectstack#6015, and #4377 has just done the same for the metadata-admin designer's own table. This literal is in neither, so it keeps `...`. Same-screen visible in the same way both of those were: the dialog renders inside the console shell beside placeholders that now end in `…`.

Fixing (1) subsumes (2) — a pack key carries whatever glyph each locale wants — so this should not be fixed as a two-character glyph edit.

## Why no gate sees it

`packages/i18n/src/__tests__/ellipsis-glyph-3878.test.ts` scans pack values and says so in its own header; this string is not in a pack. `check-i18n-call-site-keys.mjs` reads `t()` calls and their options object; there is no `t()` call here to read. `all-locales-key-parity` and `check-i18n-en-drift.mjs` likewise never see a string that exists in no pack.

## Not a duplicate of #4375

#4375 covers two call sites that **assemble** a placeholder as `t(key) + '...'` (`plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:2829`, `fields/src/widgets/LookupField.tsx:1085`). Those have a translated stem and a concatenated literal. This one has no `t()` at all — the whole string is a literal. Different shape, different fix, third site.

## Adjacent, lower-value

`examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-form-select/with-placeholder.json` sets `"placeholder": "Select..."`. That is an example schema demonstrating the `placeholder` prop, so the string is sample authored metadata rather than product copy — worth re-spelling to `…` if someone is in the file, but it is not the same defect and does not need its own card.

## Anchor

Verified on `origin/main` at `079f15571`. Related: #4024 (hardcoded-English family), #4375 (the concatenation shape), #3878 / objectstack#6015 (the ellipsis ruling), #4377 (the designer table).
